dedupe_keys.name: irf kiruna geophysical observatory magnetometer data and k index swedish institute of space physics

description: The Kiruna geophysical observatory of the Swedish Institute of Space Physics publishes magnetometer data at 68 degrees north. The magnetogram page shows the geomagnetic field in real time for the last 9 and 24 hours and daily plots back to 1970, solar quiet curves since 1978, and a preliminary real-time K index for the last three hours and a Q index for the last 15 minutes, with K computed by the Häggström and FMI methods. Real-time digital data is offered as text files for the last hour and last day, as X, Y and Z deflections in nanotesla or in IAGA format at 1-minute and 1-second resolution, for the primary and a backup magnetometer. The observatory data pages also list the primary magnetometer (installed in 2019, data from December 2020), the secondary magnetometer with data from 1990, K-index tables from 1962, the Tormestorp magnetometer at 56 degrees north (data from 2018), total field and pulsation measurements, riometers, ionosondes and a data licence page. Access is free online; the terms are on the observatory's data licence page, which was not read. Caveats: real-time values are unprocessed and may contain man-made signals, and some stations had technical problems. Coverage is northern Sweden, with a southern station. It supports geomagnetically induced current analysis for Nordic power grids and pipelines; related records are Intermagnet, the Tromsø Geophysical Observatory data and the GeoNet geomagnetic data.
